steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The biological approach assumes all behaviour has a physical cause in the brain, nervous system, genes and biochemistry. Behaviour can be explained in terms of biological structures and processes. | Key Fact: Genetic basis of behaviour: genes inherited from parents influence characteristics. Twin studies compare MZ (identical, 100% genes shared) with DZ (fraternal, 50% shared) twins. If MZ concordance is higher, genetic influence is likely. Example: McGuffin et al. found 37% MZ vs 15% DZ concordance for depression. | Key Fact: Evolution and behaviour: behaviours that enhanced survival and reproduction were naturally selected. Evolutionary explanations account for: fight-or-flight (adaptive for physical threats), attachment (infants who stayed close to caregivers survived), phobia

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe the key assumptions of the biological approach and explain how genes influence behaviour. | Evaluate the biological approach, considering its strengths and limitations. | Discuss whether behaviour is determined by biology, referring to the nature-nurture debate.
